cases.name: springmeyer-broad-based
cases.description: Broad-based weighted average on the Springmeyer example: CP2 = $2.00 × (12,000,000 + 5,000,000/2.00) / (12,000,000 + 5,000,000) = $1.7059; the 4,000,000 preferred convert to 4,689,606 shares (the article's "roughly 4.69 million").
cases.source: Bryan Springmeyer, "Anti-Dilution Provisions in Venture Capital Transactions" (https://www.calstartuplawfirm.com/business-lawyer-blog/anti-dilution-provisions.php, verified 2026-10-01)

cases.name: springmeyer-narrow-based
cases.description: Narrow-based weighted average on the same facts, base = only the series' 4,000,000 as-converted shares: CP2 = $2.00 × (4,000,000 + 2,500,000) / (4,000,000 + 5,000,000) = $1.4444; conversion yields 5,538,631 shares (the article's "5.54 million").
cases.source: Bryan Springmeyer, "Anti-Dilution Provisions in Venture Capital Transactions" (https://www.calstartuplawfirm.com/business-lawyer-blog/anti-dilution-provisions.php, verified 2026-10-01)

cases.name: springmeyer-full-ratchet
cases.description: Full ratchet on the same facts drops the conversion price to the $1.00 issue price: the Series A investor can convert their $8 million position into 8,000,000 shares.
cases.source: Bryan Springmeyer, "Anti-Dilution Provisions in Venture Capital Transactions" (https://www.calstartuplawfirm.com/business-lawyer-blog/anti-dilution-provisions.php, verified 2026-10-01)

cases.name: cooley-full-ratchet
cases.description: The Cooley GO full-ratchet example: 1,000 shares bought at $10.00; a $5.00 down round (100,000 shares for $500,000) converts the $10,000 investment into 2,000 shares.
cases.source: Cooley GO, "What You Need to Know About Down Round Financings" (https://www.cooleygo.com/down-round-financings/, verified 2026-10-01)

cases.name: springmeyer-up-round-no-adjustment
cases.description: The Springmeyer up-round (5,000,000 shares at $4.00 = $20,000,000, above the $2.00 conversion price) adjusts nothing: the conversion price stays $2.00.
cases.source: Bryan Springmeyer, "Anti-Dilution Provisions in Venture Capital Transactions" (https://www.calstartuplawfirm.com/business-lawyer-blog/anti-dilution-provisions.php, verified 2026-10-01)
